subject: Residency acceptance criteria and short-hop fallback — decision log
messages:
From: Kiran Shah <kiran.shah@medlynx.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@medlynx.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 08:12:00 +01:00
Subject: Residency acceptance criteria + short-hop fallback question

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement checklist we're capturing explicit acceptance criteria for any residency/pinning commitment before legal will sign the DPA. Two quick asks so we can move to contract review:

1) Can you provide a concise checklist of operational and telemetry evidence you require us to accept Redwood's EU residency offering (what Ops will validate before marking the account as "EU-pinned")?

2) We need clarity on the short-hop / transient failover behaviour: if there is a temporary routing to a non-EU region for <72 hours, what telemetry + notification cadence will Redwood provide, and what controls exist to limit analytic/telemetry egress? Specifically:
   - Which telemetry types (metrics, request traces, debug logs) might leave the EU during a failover?
   - Are audit logs or tokenized request traces kept only inside EU?

We attached a draft of our DPA to this mail (MedLynx_DPA_draft_v1.pdf).

If you can share the acceptance checklist and a short-runbook for transient failover, we can pass to Legal and Ops here and schedule a short call to close open items.

Thanks,
Kiran Shah
Head of Platform Security
MedLynx Health

Attachment: MedLynx_DPA_draft_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kiran Shah <kiran.shah@medlynx.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 13:05:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Residency acceptance criteria + short-hop fallback question

Kiran —

Appreciate the clear asks and the DPA draft. High-level response below; attaching our standard residency acceptance checklist and a short-runbook stub for transient/hop scenarios.

Accepted approach (summary):
- Residency acceptance is a 3-step checklist: contract (DPA + annex), operational proof (telemetry export sample + KMS key control confirmation), and a runbook review with Ops.
- For transient failovers (<72h): we provide immediate alerting (pager + email), daily telemetry export summary to your security mailbox, and a post-incident processing report that enumerates any non-EU egress artifacts.

Telemetry specifics:
- Metrics (in aggregate) may be routed to the failover region for short periods; individual request bodies are NOT persisted outside the EU in normal operations.
- Debug traces that contain request payloads are redacted by default; if debug-level traces are required they will be captured only with your explicit opt-in and stored per the DPA annex.
- Audit logs (authentication events, config changes, model-version access) are retained in the EU for the retention window agreed in the DPA; transient copies may be available to ops in the failover region for incident response but are purged within 48 hours after restoration unless you request retention for an active investigation.

Requested next steps:
1) Please confirm whether MedLynx requires KMS key escrow or split-key arrangements for the EU pinning acceptance — that impacts the acceptance checklist item 2.
2) If you can share 2–3 sample queries/telemetry channels your Ops team wants us to include in the acceptance report, we'll bake those into the runbook.

Attachments: redwood_residency_acceptance_checklist.pdf, residency_runbook_stub.txt

I'll loop in Kimberly for legal specifics.

— Jonas
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Jonas — a few clarifications from Contracts/Legal:

- MedLynx prefers a split-KMS model (customer-managed key + Redwood envelope key). Can Redwood confirm support and provide a short ops flow for rotating or revoking keys without service disruption?

- For the acceptance report, we need assurance that any telemetry exported during failover cannot be correlated back to PII (we will supply a sample of the telemetry channels).

- We also want a visible owner and SLA for the post-incident processing report (name & escalation path).

Can Marissa confirm the ops owner and an SLA target (we are proposing 5 business days for the initial processing report, 15 business days for a full evidence package)?

— Contracts (on behalf of MedLynx)
